title: Making plans with friends
goal: Ask a friend if they're free, suggest what to do, fix a time and place, say you're on your way or running late, and cancel without upsetting anyone.
intro:
Welcome to Part 2. From here on the course is about the Kannada you'll use with friends and around town, and it starts with the most common conversation of all: **making plans**. Are you free? Shall we go out? Where shall we meet? I'm on my way. Sorry, stuck in traffic. Let's do another day.

With friends your age you'll use **ನೀನು** and the bare verb, and this unit adds the warm extras young Kannadigas use with each other: **ಬಾರೋ / ಬಾರೇ** 'come on', **ಕಣೋ / ಕಣೇ** 'I'm telling you', **ಮಗಾ** 'dude'. You'll also practise **-ಓಣ** 'let's' and **-ಓಣ್ವಾ?** 'shall we?', the ways to say 'I'm off', 'on my way' and 'about to', and the English words everyone in Bengaluru drops into plans: **ಫ್ರೀ, ಪ್ಲಾನ್, ಲೇಟ್, ಟ್ರಾಫಿಕ್, ಕ್ಯಾನ್ಸಲ್**.

vocab.note: From English. ಫ್ರೀ ಇದ್ದೀಯಾ? 'are you free?'
The Kannada word: ನಿನಗೆ ಬಿಡುವಿದೆಯಾ? 'do you have time?' (a little more careful than ಫ್ರೀ).
ಪ್ಲಾನ್ ಮಾಡು 'to plan'. Native word: ಯೋಜನೆ (unit 17), which sounds formal in chat.
From English. ಬೋರ್ ಆಗ್ತಿದೆ 'I'm bored' (lit. it's becoming boring); ಬೋರ್ ಹೊಡೆಸ್ತಿದೆ 'it's so boring'.
Spoken ಎಲ್ಲಾದ್ರೂ ellādrū. 'Nowhere' = ಎಲ್ಲೂ + negative: ಎಲ್ಲೂ ಹೋಗಲ್ಲ.

vocab.en: to go around, wander about, hang out
vocab.note: ಊರು ಸುತ್ತಾಡು 'to go around town'.
Metro stations and malls have numbered gates: ಗೇಟ್ ನಂಬರ್ ಎರಡು.
After the noun: ಮಾಲ್ ಎದುರು 'opposite the mall'.
ಪಕ್ಕಾ? 'for sure?' — ಪಕ್ಕಾ! 'definitely!'
From ಹೊತ್ತು 'time': ಏಳು ಗಂಟೆ ಹೊತ್ತಿಗೆ 'by seven'.
Spoken ಕರ್ಕೊಂಡು ಬಾ 'bring (them) along'. For things use ತರು.
From English, the everyday word for a friend of either sex; plural ಫ್ರೆಂಡ್ಸ್. Kannada: ಸ್ನೇಹಿತ (m), ಸ್ನೇಹಿತೆ (f), ಗೆಳೆಯ / ಗೆಳತಿ.
Literally 'son!'. Bengaluru slang between young men; joking, warm, and too familiar for anyone else.
At the end of a statement to a male friend: ಹೌದು ಕಣೋ 'yeah, man'. To a woman ಕಣೇ; more respectful ಕಣ್ರೀ.

vocab.en: uncle (polite address to an older man, e.g. a friend's father)
vocab.note: From English. A woman of that age is ಆಂಟಿ āṇṭi. Both always get ನೀವು forms.
The person reminded is in the dative: ನನಗೆ ನೆನಪಿಸು 'remind me'. Spoken also ನೆನಪು ಮಾಡು.
Past ಹೊರಟ- (irregular): ಹೊರಟೆ 'I left / I'm off'. Present ಹೊರಡ್ತೀನಿ.
With the future: ಇನ್ನೇನು ಬರ್ತಾನೆ 'he'll be here any minute'.
ಹೇಗೂ ನಾಳೆ ರಜೆ 'tomorrow's a holiday anyway'.
From English. ಲೇಟ್ ಆಗುತ್ತೆ 'I'll be late'; ಲೇಟಾಗಿ 'late (adv)'. Kannada: ತಡ.
Spoken with locative: ಟ್ರಾಫಿಕ್ಕಲ್ಲಿ 'in traffic'.
Spoken ಸಿಕ್ಕಾಕೊಳ್ಳು: ಸಿಕ್ಕಾಕೊಂಡಿದ್ದೀನಿ 'I'm stuck'.
ಕ್ಯಾನ್ಸಲ್ ಮಾಡು 'to cancel', ಕ್ಯಾನ್ಸಲ್ ಆಯ್ತು 'it got cancelled'. Kannada: ರದ್ದು.
From English. Kannada: ತುರ್ತು.
Spoken also ಪೋಸ್ಟ್‌ಪೋನ್ ಮಾಡು.

phrases.native: ಮೆಟ್ರೋ ಸ್ಟೇಷನ್ ಗೇಟ್ ಹತ್ರ ಏಳು ಗಂಟೆಗೆ ಸಿಗೋಣ
phrases.roman: meṭrō sṭēshan gēṭ hatra ēḷu gaṇṭege sigōṇa
phrases.en: Let's meet at seven at the metro station gate.

phrases.note: Literally 'I left'. Said as you walk out of the door.

phrases.en: I'm nearly there. (I'll be there any minute)
Sorry, I'll be a bit late.

phrases.native: ಇವತ್ತು ಆಗಲ್ಲ ಕಣೋ, ಇನ್ನೊಂದು ದಿನ ಮಾಡೋಣ
phrases.roman: ivattu āgalla kaṇō, innondu dina māḍōṇa
phrases.en: Can't make it today, man, let's do another day.
Come on, hurry up! (to a male friend)
phrases.note: To a female friend: ಬಾರೇ, ಬೇಗ!

grammar.title: Let's… and shall we…?
grammar.body:
**Let's** = verb stem + **-ಓಣ** (unit 11): ಹೋಗೋಣ 'let's go', ತಿನ್ನೋಣ 'let's eat', ಸಿಗೋಣ 'let's meet', ಹೊರಡೋಣ 'let's leave'. Verbs in -ಇ/-ಎ add -ಯೋಣ: ಕುಡಿಯೋಣ 'let's drink'. It always includes you, so it's the natural way to suggest anything to a friend or a group.

**Shall we?** = add the question **-ಆ**: **-ಓಣ್ವಾ?** (careful ಹೋಗೋಣವಾ?): ಸಿನಿಮಾಗೆ ಹೋಗೋಣ್ವಾ? 'shall we go to a film?'

**Where / when / what shall we...?** = question word + -ಓಣ, with no -ಆ: ಎಲ್ಲಿ ಸಿಗೋಣ? 'where shall we meet?', ಎಷ್ಟು ಗಂಟೆಗೆ ಹೊರಡೋಣ? 'what time shall we leave?', ಏನು ಮಾಡೋಣ? 'what shall we do?'

**Come on, let's...** = ಬಾ (or ನಡಿ 'move!') + -ಓಣ: ಬಾ, ಹೋಗೋಣ; ನಡಿ, ತಿನ್ನೋಣ.

**Let's not** = verbal noun + **ಬೇಡ**: ಇವತ್ತು ಹೋಗೋದು ಬೇಡ 'let's not go today' (lit. going is not wanted). Don't say ಹೋಗೋಣ ಇಲ್ಲ.

**Why don't we...?** = ಯಾಕೆ + infinitive + **-ಬಾರದು**: ಮೈಸೂರಿಗೆ ಯಾಕೆ ಹೋಗಬಾರದು? 'why don't we go to Mysuru?' (lit. why shouldn't we go?).

**Maybe / let's see** = **ನೋಡೋಣ**. Be warned: a friend who answers ನೋಡೋಣ is often politely saying no.

**Saying yes**: ಸರಿ, ಓಕೆ, ಆಯ್ತು, ಹೋಗೋಣ, or ಪಕ್ಕಾ! 'definitely!'

examples.en: Shall we go somewhere on Saturday?
Come on, let's have a coffee.

examples.native: ಇವತ್ತು ಹೊರಗೆ ಹೋಗೋದು ಬೇಡ, ಮಳೆ ಬರ್ತಿದೆ
examples.roman: ivattu horage hōgōdu bēḍa, maḷe bartide
examples.en: Let's not go out today, it's raining.
Why don't we go to Nandi Hills?

grammar.title: Talking to friends: ನೀನು commands, -ಓ / -ಏ and ಕಣೋ
grammar.body:
With friends you use the **ನೀನು** forms, and the command is the bare verb stem (unit 11): ಬಾ 'come', ಹೋಗು 'go', ಹೇಳು 'tell', ನೋಡು 'look', ಇರು 'wait, hang on'. 'Don't' = infinitive + **-ಬೇಡ**: ಲೇಟ್ ಮಾಡಬೇಡ 'don't be late', ಮರೀಬೇಡ 'don't forget' (careful ಮರೆಯಬೇಡ).

**The friendly -ಓ / -ಏ.** Young people add **-ಓ** when talking to a man and **-ಏ** to a woman. It replaces the final -ಉ, and ಬಾ adds ರ:
ಬಾ → **ಬಾರೋ** / **ಬಾರೇ** 'come on'
ಹೇಳು → **ಹೇಳೋ** / **ಹೇಳೇ** 'tell me'
ಹೋಗು → **ಹೋಗೋ** / **ಹೋಗೇ** 'go on; get lost (joking)'
To a group of friends: **-ರೋ**: ಬನ್ರೋ 'come on, guys'. These sound warm between friends and rude to anyone else.

**ಕಣೋ / ಕಣೇ** at the end of a statement means 'I'm telling you' and makes it friendlier and more insistent: ಹೌದು ಕಣೋ 'yeah, man', ಬರ್ತೀನಿ ಕಣೇ 'I'm coming, I promise'. With an older person who's still informal with you, ಕಣ್ರೀ.

**Just do it**: past participle + **ಬಿಡು** (unit 23 has more): ಹೇಳ್ಬಿಡು 'just tell me', ಬಂದ್ಬಿಡು 'just come over'.

**When to switch back**: a friend's parents, anyone noticeably older, a shopkeeper, a new colleague all get the polite forms: ಬನ್ನಿ, ಹೇಳಿ, ಕೂತ್ಕೊಳ್ಳಿ, ಮರೀಬೇಡಿ.

examples.en: Come on, man, the film's started!
Tell me, what's the plan? (to a female friend)

examples.native: ಲೇಟ್ ಮಾಡಬೇಡ, ಸಿನಿಮಾ ಆರು ಗಂಟೆಗೆ ಶುರು
examples.roman: lēṭ māḍabēḍa, sinimā āru gaṇṭege shuru
examples.en: Don't be late, the film starts at six.

grammar.title: I'm off, on my way, about to: ಹೊರಟೆ, ದಾರಿಯಲ್ಲಿದ್ದೀನಿ, ಇನ್ನೇನು
grammar.body:
**Leaving this second.** Kannada uses the **past** for something that is starting right now, as if it were already done: **ಹೊರಟೆ!** 'I'm off!', **ಬಂದೆ!** 'coming!' (shouted to someone who's calling you). The present continuous says the same less dramatically: ಹೊರಡ್ತಿದ್ದೀನಿ 'I'm leaving now'.

**Already set off.** Present perfect: ಹೊರಟಿದ್ದೀನಿ 'I've set off', ಇನ್ನೂ ಹೊರಟಿಲ್ಲ 'haven't left yet'.

**On the way.** ದಾರಿಯಲ್ಲಿದ್ದೀನಿ (fast ದಾರೀಲಿದ್ದೀನಿ) 'I'm on the way'; ಬರ್ತಿದ್ದೀನಿ 'I'm coming'. Friends know that ಬರ್ತಿದ್ದೀನಿ sometimes means 'I'm about to get in the shower'.

**Any minute now.** **ಇನ್ನೇನು** + future: ಇನ್ನೇನು ತಲುಪ್ತೀನಿ 'I'll be there any minute', ಸಿನಿಮಾ ಇನ್ನೇನು ಶುರು ಆಗುತ್ತೆ 'the film's about to start'.

**Was about to (when...).** Verbal noun + **-ಅಲ್ಲಿದ್ದೆ**: ಹೊರಡೋದ್ರಲ್ಲಿದ್ದೆ 'I was just about to leave' (careful ಹೊರಡುವುದರಲ್ಲಿದ್ದೆ). Follow it with ಅಷ್ಟರಲ್ಲಿ for the interruption: ಹೊರಡೋದ್ರಲ್ಲಿದ್ದೆ, ಅಷ್ಟರಲ್ಲಿ ಮಳೆ ಬಂತು.

**By a time.** ಹೊತ್ತಿಗೆ: ಏಳು ಗಂಟೆ ಹೊತ್ತಿಗೆ ಬರ್ತೀನಿ 'I'll be there by seven'.

**Late is something that happens.** ಲೇಟ್ ಆಗುತ್ತೆ 'I'll be late' (lit. it will become late), ನನಗೆ ಲೇಟ್ ಆಯ್ತು 'I'm late', ನಿನಗೆ ಯಾಕೆ ಲೇಟ್ ಆಯ್ತು? 'why are you late?'. The trap: ನಾನು ಲೇಟ್ ✗. Being stuck is a state, so it takes the perfect: ಸಿಕ್ಕಾಕೊಂಡಿದ್ದೀನಿ 'I'm stuck' (I've got stuck).

examples.en: I'm off! I'll be there in twenty minutes.
She's on her way, she'll be here any minute.

examples.native: ನಾನು ಹೊರಡೋದ್ರಲ್ಲಿದ್ದೆ, ಅಷ್ಟರಲ್ಲಿ ಅಮ್ಮ ಫೋನ್ ಮಾಡಿದ್ರು
examples.roman: nānu horaḍōdrallidde, aṣṭaralli amma phōn māḍidru
examples.en: I was just about to leave when Mum called.

dialogue.title: Saturday in Indiranagar
dialogue.setting: On Thursday Arjun calls his friend Sneha to plan Saturday. Then it's Saturday, 6:15 pm, and everyone is waiting at the metro station.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.native: ಹಲೋ ಸ್ನೇಹಾ, ಶನಿವಾರ ಸಂಜೆ ಫ್ರೀ ಇದ್ದೀಯಾ?
lines.roman: halō snēhā, shanivāra sañje phrī iddīyā?
lines.en: Hello Sneha, are you free on Saturday evening?

lines.speaker: Sneha
lines.native: ಹೂಂ, ಇದ್ದೀನಿ ಅನ್ಸುತ್ತೆ. ಯಾಕೆ, ಏನ್ ಪ್ಲಾನ್?
lines.roman: hūṃ, iddīni ansutte. yāke, ēn plān?
lines.en: Mm, I think so. Why, what's the plan?

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.native: ಎಲ್ಲಾ ಫ್ರೆಂಡ್ಸ್ ಒಟ್ಟಿಗೆ ಇಂದಿರಾನಗರದಲ್ಲಿ ಸುತ್ತಾಡೋಣ ಅಂತ. ಆಮೇಲೆ ಊಟ.
lines.roman: ellā phreṇḍs oṭṭige indirānagaradalli suttāḍōṇa anta. āmēle ūṭa.
lines.en: We thought the whole gang could hang out in Indiranagar. Then dinner.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.native: ಇಂದಿರಾನಗರ ಮೆಟ್ರೋ ಸ್ಟೇಷನ್ ಗೇಟ್ ಹತ್ರ, ಆರು ಗಂಟೆಗೆ. ಪಕ್ಕಾ ಬರ್ತೀಯಾ?
lines.roman: indirānagara meṭrō sṭēshan gēṭ hatra, āru gaṇṭege. pakkā bartīyā?
lines.en: At the Indiranagar metro station gate, at six. You're definitely coming?

lines.speaker: Sneha
lines.native: ಪಕ್ಕಾ ಕಣೋ. ಶನಿವಾರ ಬೆಳಿಗ್ಗೆ ನನಗೆ ನೆನಪಿಸು, ಆಯ್ತಾ?
lines.roman: pakkā kaṇō. shanivāra beḷigge nanage nenapisu, āytā?
lines.en: Definitely. Remind me on Saturday morning, OK?

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.en: Where are you? We're all waiting at the gate!

lines.speaker: Sneha
lines.native: ಸಾರಿ ಸಾರಿ! ಹೊರಟೆ, ದಾರಿಯಲ್ಲಿದ್ದೀನಿ. ಸಿಲ್ಕ್ ಬೋರ್ಡ್ ಹತ್ರ ಟ್ರಾಫಿಕ್ಕಲ್ಲಿ ಸಿಕ್ಕಾಕೊಂಡಿದ್ದೀನಿ.
lines.roman: sāri sāri! horaṭe, dāriyalliddīni. silk bōrḍ hatra ṭrāphikkalli sikkākoṇḍiddīni.
lines.en: Sorry, sorry! I've left, I'm on my way. I'm stuck in traffic near Silk Board.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.native: ಸಿಲ್ಕ್ ಬೋರ್ಡಾ? ಅಯ್ಯೋ, ಹಾಗಾದ್ರೆ ಇನ್ನೂ ಒಂದು ಗಂಟೆ!
lines.roman: silk bōrḍā? ayyō, hāgādre innū ondu gaṇṭe!
lines.en: Silk Board? Oh no, then that's another hour!

lines.speaker: Sneha
lines.native: ಇಲ್ಲ ಕಣೋ, ಆಟೋ ಬಿಟ್ಟು ಮೆಟ್ರೋದಲ್ಲಿ ಬರ್ತೀನಿ. ಇನ್ನೇನು ತಲುಪ್ತೀನಿ!
lines.roman: illa kaṇō, āṭō biṭṭu meṭrōdalli bartīni. innēnu taluptīni!
lines.en: No, man, I'll ditch the auto and take the metro. I'll be there any minute!

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.native: ಸರಿ, ಬೇಗ ಬಾರೇ. ಅಷ್ಟರಲ್ಲಿ ನಾವು ಒಂದು ಕಾಫಿ ಕುಡೀತೀವಿ.
lines.roman: sari, bēga bārē. aṣṭaralli nāvu ondu kāphi kuḍītīvi.
lines.en: OK, hurry up. We'll have a coffee meanwhile.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.native: ಹಹ, ಇಲ್ಲ. ಹೇಗೂ ಟೇಬಲ್ ಬುಕ್ ಮಾಡಿದ್ದೀವಿ.
lines.roman: haha, illa. hēgū ṭēbal buk māḍiddīvi.
lines.en: Haha, no. We've booked a table anyway.

culture:
In Bengaluru every plan is built around the traffic. **Silk Board** junction is a running joke (people say they've 'aged' waiting there), and many friends now meet at a **Namma Metro** station gate because the metro is the one thing that runs on time. Weekend plans are things like a walk in Cubbon Park, Church Street or Indiranagar in the evening, a darshini breakfast, or an early drive to Nandi Hills for the sunrise. In Mysuru it's Chamundi Hills or the palace lights on a Sunday; in Mangaluru, the beach at Panambur or Tannirbhavi.

Time is elastic. **ಬಂದೆ!** 'coming!' and **ದಾರಿಯಲ್ಲಿದ್ದೀನಿ** 'on my way' are said generously, and **ನೋಡೋಣ** 'let's see' usually means 'probably not'. When you cancel, always give a reason (**ಹುಷಾರಿಲ್ಲ**, **ಅರ್ಜೆಂಟ್ ಕೆಲಸ**) and offer **ಇನ್ನೊಂದು ದಿನ** 'another day'; a flat ಬರಲ್ಲ sounds cold.

The friendly **ಬಾರೋ / ಬಾರೇ**, **ಕಣೋ / ಕಣೇ** and **ಮಗಾ** are for friends your own age. Someone a few years older gets **ಅಣ್ಣ** 'big brother' or **ಅಕ್ಕ** 'big sister' tacked on (ಬನ್ನಿ ಅಣ್ಣ), even if they're not family, and a friend's parents are **ಅಂಕಲ್** and **ಆಂಟಿ** with full ನೀವು forms.

lessons.title: Are you free? Let's go out

tip.title: Let's: -ಓಣ · Shall we?: -ಓಣ್ವಾ?
tip.body:
- **Let's** = stem + **-ಓಣ**: ಹೋಗೋಣ, ಸಿಗೋಣ, ಕುಡಿಯೋಣ.
- **Shall we?** add -ಆ: **ಹೋಗೋಣ್ವಾ?**
- **Let's not** = verbal noun + **ಬೇಡ**: ಹೋಗೋದು ಬೇಡ.
- **Why don't we...?** = ಯಾಕೆ + **-ಬಾರದು**: ಯಾಕೆ ಹೋಗಬಾರದು?
- **ನೋಡೋಣ** 'let's see' is often a polite no.

sentences.en: Shall we go to a film tomorrow evening?
I'm bored, let's go out somewhere.
Do you have any free time this weekend?
Let's all have dinner together.

sentences.native: ಇವತ್ತು ಎಲ್ಲಾದರೂ ಹೋಗೋದು ಬೇಡ, ಮನೆಯಲ್ಲೇ ಇರೋಣ.
sentences.roman: ivattu ellādarū hōgōdu bēḍa, maneyallē irōṇa.
sentences.en: Let's not go anywhere today, let's just stay home.
Why don't we go to Cubbon Park on Sunday?

sentences.native: ಇವತ್ತು ಸಂಜೆ ಫ್ರೀ ಇದ್ದೀಯಾ? ಒಂದು ಕಾಫಿ ಕುಡಿಯೋಣ.
sentences.roman: ivattu sañje phrī iddīyā? ondu kāphi kuḍiyōṇa.
sentences.en: Are you free this evening? Let's have a coffee.
OK, let's see, I'll let you know on Friday.

sentences.native: ನಾನು ಇವತ್ತು ಫ್ರೀ ಇಲ್ಲ, ನಾಳೆ ಪ್ಲಾನ್ ಮಾಡೋಣ.
sentences.roman: nānu ivattu phrī illa, nāḷe plān māḍōṇa.
sentences.en: I'm not free today, let's plan tomorrow.
What's the plan? A film or dinner?

lessons.title: Where and when shall we meet?

tip.title: Fixing a time and place
tip.body:
- **ಎಲ್ಲಿ ಸಿಗೋಣ?** 'where shall we meet?' **ಎಷ್ಟು ಗಂಟೆಗೆ?** 'what time?'
- Places: X **ಹತ್ರ** 'at / near X', X **ಎದುರು** 'opposite X', X **ಗೇಟ್ ಹತ್ರ** 'at the X gate'.
- **ಹೊತ್ತಿಗೆ** 'by (a time)': ಏಳು ಗಂಟೆ ಹೊತ್ತಿಗೆ.
- Seal it: **ಪಕ್ಕಾ?** — **ಪಕ್ಕಾ!**
- People are brought along (**ಕರ್ಕೊಂಡು ಬಾ**); things are brought (**ತಗೊಂಡು ಬಾ / ತಾ**).

tip.title: Friends' commands: ಬಾರೋ, ಹೇಳೇ, ಕಣೋ
tip.body:
- With friends: bare verb **ಬಾ, ಹೇಳು, ಇರು**; 'don't' = **-ಬೇಡ**: ಮರೀಬೇಡ.
- Friendly **-ಓ** to a man, **-ಏ** to a woman: **ಬಾರೋ / ಬಾರೇ**, **ಹೇಳೋ / ಹೇಳೇ**; to a group **ಬನ್ರೋ**.
- **ಕಣೋ / ಕಣೇ** after a statement: ಹೌದು ಕಣೋ 'yeah, man'.
- Anyone older: **ಬನ್ನಿ, ಹೇಳಿ**.

tip.title: Off, on the way, any minute
tip.body:
- Leaving this second: the past! **ಹೊರಟೆ!** 'I'm off!', **ಬಂದೆ!** 'coming!'
- On the way: **ದಾರಿಯಲ್ಲಿದ್ದೀನಿ**; coming: **ಬರ್ತಿದ್ದೀನಿ**.
- Any minute: **ಇನ್ನೇನು** + future: ಇನ್ನೇನು ತಲುಪ್ತೀನಿ.
- Was about to: **ಹೊರಡೋದ್ರಲ್ಲಿದ್ದೆ** 'I was just about to leave'.

tip.title: Late is something that happens
tip.body:
- **ಲೇಟ್ ಆಗುತ್ತೆ** 'I'll be late', **ನನಗೆ ಲೇಟ್ ಆಯ್ತು** 'I'm late': lateness *happens* to you. Not ನಾನು ಲೇಟ್.
- Stuck is a state, so use the perfect: **ಸಿಕ್ಕಾಕೊಂಡಿದ್ದೀನಿ** 'I'm stuck'.
- Say how long: **ಇನ್ನೂ ಹತ್ತು ನಿಮಿಷ ಆಗುತ್ತೆ** 'it'll be another ten minutes'.

lessons.title: Cancelling without upsetting anyone

tip.title: Saying no nicely
tip.body:
- Give a reason: **ಏನೋ ಅರ್ಜೆಂಟ್ ಕೆಲಸ ಬಂತು**, **ಹುಷಾರಿಲ್ಲ** 'I'm not well'.
- **ಇವತ್ತು ಆಗಲ್ಲ** 'I can't today' (lit. it won't happen) is softer than **ಬರಲ್ಲ** 'I won't come'.
- Offer another day: **ಇನ್ನೊಂದು ದಿನ ಮಾಡೋಣ**, **ಮುಂದಿನ ವಾರ?**
- A flat ಬರಲ್ಲ with no reason sounds cold.
